title: The Sunday Read: ‘How Many Billionaires Are There, Anyway?’

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin, and I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店打碟时，你每晚也要带上300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 然后把DJ台变成一个活生生的快闪博物馆，陈列着各种精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: I don't know if you know about the Scrub Daddy.
sentences.zh: 不知道你有没有听说过“Scrub Daddy”这款清洁海绵。

sentences.en: It's a fantastic product.
sentences.zh: 它是一款非常棒的产品。

sentences.en: It's a little yellow piece of synthetic steel wool with a big smiley face on it, and it's for scrubbing pots and pans and whatever else.
sentences.zh: 它是一块黄色的小型合成钢丝棉，上面有一个大大的笑脸，专门用来刷锅碗瓢盆以及其他各种东西。

sentences.en: And I didn't know this until I started sitting down to write this story, but it was actually introduced to the world via Shark Tank, the show on ABC.
sentences.zh: 在准备写这个故事之前，我并不知道它其实是通过ABC电视台的节目《创智赢家》推向世界的。

sentences.en: Hi, sharks.
sentences.zh: 鲨鱼们，你们好。

sentences.en: I'm Aaron Krause from Philadelphia, and I'm known as the daddy of the scrub daddy, the cutest but most high-tech scrubbing tool in the world.
sentences.zh: 我是来自费城的亚伦·克劳斯，我被称为“Scrub Daddy之父”，这是世界上最可爱但科技含量最高的清洁工具。

sentences.en: It's a popular show where people with small businesses come before a panel of the sharks, and they have to make a pitch to them, these ultra-wealthy investors.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很受欢迎的节目，小企业主们来到由“鲨鱼”组成的投资人小组面前，向这些超级富有的投资者进行推介。

sentences.en: It's this fantasy ritual in which you get to witness the capitalist class investing in small American businesses and making them grow and bringing their expertise as wealthy capitalists to bear on these small,
sentences.zh: 这是一种梦幻般的仪式，你可以亲眼目睹资本家阶层投资美国小企业，帮助它们成长，并运用他们作为富有资本家的专业知识，去支持这些小型、

sentences.en: struggling businesses that need capital and expertise.
sentences.zh: 苦苦挣扎且需要资金和专业知识的企业。

sentences.en: But this is not what most people like Mark Cuban are doing.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是像马克·库班这样的人大多数时候在做的事情。

sentences.en: You know, for the most part, our billionaires come out of technology, out of finance.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在很大程度上，我们的亿万富翁大多来自科技界和金融界。

sentences.en: They are not in the business of investing in small businesses.
sentences.zh: 他们并不从事投资小企业的业务。

sentences.en: That's not how people are getting ultra-wealthy in this country anymore.
sentences.zh: 在这个国家，这已经不再是人们变得超级富有的方式了。

sentences.en: I'll go to 20.
sentences.zh: 我出到20。

sentences.zh: 成交。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: My name is Willie Staley, and I'm a story editor at the New York Times Magazine.
sentences.zh: 我叫威利·斯泰利，是《纽约时报杂志》的故事编辑。

sentences.en: For a money issue, we wanted to take a look at the billionaire class and what it means to live in a society that feels increasingly dominated by billionaires.
sentences.zh: 为了做一期关于金钱的专题，我们想审视一下亿万富翁阶层，以及生活在一个感觉日益被亿万富翁主宰的社会中意味着什么。

sentences.en: The number of billionaires has been growing, and it's been growing rather quickly here in the United States.
sentences.zh: 亿万富翁的数量一直在增长，而且在美国增长得相当快。

sentences.en: In 2002, Forbes estimated there were 243 billionaires in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 2002年，《福布斯》估计美国有243位亿万富翁。

sentences.en: Ten years later, in 2012, it was 424 billionaires in the United States.
sentences.zh: 十年后的2012年，美国有424位亿万富翁。

sentences.en: And now, in 2022, their latest count is 735.
sentences.zh: 而现在，在2022年，他们最新的统计数字是735位。

sentences.en: Our question was, why do we have so many billionaires, and where do they come from?
sentences.zh: 我们的问题是，为什么我们会有这么多亿万富翁，他们是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: So a billion is a hard number to wrap your head around, and we tried to work with this in the issue.
sentences.zh: “十亿”是一个很难想象的数字，我们在这一期节目中尝试去解读它。

sentences.en: It's a thousand millions.
sentences.zh: 那是1000个百万。

sentences.en: One million seconds is 12 days, and a billion seconds is 31 years.
sentences.zh: 一百万秒是12天，而十亿秒是31年。

sentences.en: So, I mean, if you have in your head how big one billion is, imagine that Jeff Bezos, who's not even the richest person on the planet currently, has 177 of those.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，如果你脑子里对十亿有多大有个概念，想象一下杰夫·贝佐斯——他甚至还不是目前地球上最富有的人——拥有177个十亿。

sentences.en: That's as of this morning.
sentences.zh: 这是截至今天早上的数据。

sentences.en: We had these illustrations done by this great illustrator, Mona Chalabi, who thought of creative ways to imagine what Jeff Bezos' net worth is.
sentences.zh: 我们请了伟大的插画家莫娜·查拉比绘制了这些插图，她想出了各种有创意的方式来想象杰夫·贝佐斯的净资产。

sentences.en: And one of my favorites was that the average full-time Amazon employee made $37,930 in 2020.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的一个例子是：2020年亚马逊全职员工的平均年薪为37,930美元。

sentences.en: In order to accumulate as much wealth as Jeff Bezos, someone earning that salary would have had to start working in the Pleocene epoch.
sentences.zh: 为了积累像杰夫·贝佐斯那么多的财富，一个拿着这份薪水的人必须从上新世就开始工作了。

sentences.en: So that's basically 4.5 million years ago when early hominids were appearing on Earth.
sentences.zh: 那基本上是450万年前，早期人类出现在地球上的时候。

sentences.en: Billionaires are certainly an expression of the promise of American enterprise on the one hand in the free market system, but at the same time,
sentences.zh: 亿万富翁一方面确实是美国企业精神和自由市场体系的体现，但与此同时，

sentences.en: a really profound illustration of how unequal the spoils have been split over the last four decades.
sentences.zh: 这也是过去四十年来财富分配极度不平等的一个深刻写照。

sentences.en: You can think of it as an extremely anti-democratic accumulation of power, because their whims can be satisfied much more easily than the rest of us,
sentences.zh: 你可以把它看作是一种极端的反民主的权力积累，因为他们的心血来潮比我们其他人更容易得到满足，

sentences.en: and their whims might be to become the president, for example.
sentences.zh: 而他们心血来潮想做的事，比如成为总统。

sentences.en: And we've seen this over and over again.
sentences.zh: 我们已经一次又一次地看到了这一点。

sentences.en: Elon Musk loves posting more than anyone, and all of a sudden he decided he would just buy Twitter and try to run it his way.
sentences.zh: 埃隆·马斯克比任何人都喜欢发帖，突然之间，他决定买下推特，并尝试按自己的方式去经营它。

sentences.en: He has $250 billion at his disposal, and he can just do this sort of thing at the drop of a hat.
sentences.zh: 他拥有2500亿美元的资产，可以随心所欲地做这类事情。

sentences.en: And I think that's the crazy-making aspect of living in a society that has so many billionaires.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是生活在一个拥有如此多亿万富翁的社会中令人抓狂的地方。

sentences.en: They can use their money to make decisions about what exists and what doesn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 他们可以用自己的钱来决定什么东西存在，什么东西不存在。

sentences.en: So here's my article, How Many Billionaires Are There Anyway?
sentences.zh: 这是我的文章，《到底有多少亿万富翁？》

sentences.zh: 由埃里克·杰森·马丁朗读。

sentences.zh: 由Autumn录制。

sentences.zh: 想在智能手机上收听更多来自《纽约时报》、《纽约客》、《名利场》、《大西洋月刊》及其他出版物的故事，

sentences.zh: 访问autumn，即A-U-D-M点com了解更多详情。

sentences.en: In 1981, Malcolm Forbes, the eccentric and fabulously wealthy magazine publisher, came to his editors with a requeSt.
sentences.zh: 1981年，古怪且极其富有的杂志出版商马尔科姆·福布斯向他的编辑们提出了一个要求。

sentences.en: Could they pull together a special issue about the 400 richest Americans?
sentences.zh: 他们能否整理出一期关于美国400位最富有者的特刊？

sentences.en: The idea was inspired by Caroline Schirmerhorn Astor, the doyen of Gilded Age New York, who regularly hosted the city's high society in her Fifth Avenue ballroom,
sentences.zh: 这个想法的灵感来自于镀金时代纽约的名媛卡罗琳·舍默霍恩·阿斯特，她经常在自己第五大道的宴会厅里招待城中的上流社会，
zh_words: 卡罗琳·舍默霍恩·阿斯特

sentences.en: which was said to fit about 400 people.
sentences.zh: 据说那里大约能容纳400人。

sentences.en: It's quite possible Forbes saw something of himself in Astor.
sentences.zh: 福布斯很可能在阿斯特身上看到了自己的影子。

sentences.en: This was a different era of magazine publishing.
sentences.zh: 那是一个不同的杂志出版时代。

sentences.en: Forbes, who wound up making the cut on his own list, lived like a sultan.
sentences.zh: 最终也把自己列入榜单的福布斯，过着苏丹般的生活。

sentences.en: He entertained celebrities and politicians on a 126-foot yacht called The Highlander.
sentences.zh: 他在一艘名为“高地人号”的126英尺游艇上招待名人和政客。

sentences.en: By the end of his run, he owned a chateau in Normandy, 12 Fabergé eggs, and a collection of hot air balloons in fantastical designs.
sentences.zh: 在他职业生涯的末期，他拥有一座诺曼底的城堡、12枚法贝热彩蛋，以及一系列造型奇幻的热气球。

sentences.en: One shaped like the Sphinx, one like the Sphinx, one like a bust of Beethoven, one like a Fabergé egg, one like the chateau in Normandy, and, of course,
sentences.zh: 一个形状像狮身人面像，一个像贝多芬的半身像，一个像法贝热彩蛋，一个像诺曼底的城堡，当然，

sentences.en: one in the image of a sultan, about as tall as his yacht was long.
sentences.zh: 还有一个苏丹形象的，高度几乎和他游艇的长度一样。

sentences.en: According to a brief history of the magazine, written by Malcolm Forbes, Jr., better known as Steve, the editorial staff was not pleased with his father's idea.
sentences.zh: 据马尔科姆·福布斯二世（即史蒂夫）所写的杂志简史记载，编辑部对父亲的想法并不满意。

sentences.en: They conducted a feasibility study and told him it wouldn't be possible to figure out who these 400 people were.
sentences.zh: 他们进行了可行性研究，并告诉他，要弄清楚这400个人是谁是不可能的。

sentences.en: The elder Forbes replied, if they wouldn't do it, he'd find some other journalists who could.
sentences.zh: 老福布斯回答说，如果他们不干，他会找其他能干的记者来做。

sentences.en: Edit capitulated, writes his son.
sentences.zh: “编辑部屈服了，”他的儿子写道。

sentences.en: The resulting reporting project took a year, dozens of flights, and thousands of interviews.
sentences.zh: 随后的报道项目耗时一年，进行了数十次飞行和数千次采访。

sentences.en: At the top of the very first Forbes 400 list was Daniel K.
sentences.zh: 在第一份《福布斯》400富豪榜榜首的是丹尼尔·K·

sentences.en: Ludwig, a shipping magnate, estimated by the magazine to be worth more than $2 billion.
sentences.zh: 路德维希，一位航运大亨，杂志估计其身家超过20亿美元。

sentences.en: If you simply adjusted for inflation, that's now at least $5.8 billion, a fortune that would land Ludwig in a seven-way tie for the 182nd spot on the last Forbes 400 list,
sentences.zh: 如果简单地根据通货膨胀进行调整，那现在至少是58亿美元，这笔财富会让路德维希在上一份《福布斯》400富豪榜上并列第182位，

sentences.en: alongside Fred Smith, the founder of FedEx, Gary Rollins, chief executive of Rollins Incorporated, which owns several pest control companies,
sentences.zh: 与联邦快递创始人弗雷德·史密斯、拥有多家害虫防治公司的罗林斯公司首席执行官加里·罗林斯并列，

sentences.en: and who could forget Peter Gassner, the head of a cloud software company called Viva.
sentences.zh: 还有谁能忘记云软件公司Viva的负责人彼得·加斯纳呢。

sentences.en: Fortunes at this tier hardly seem to merit media coverage anymore.
sentences.zh: 这个层级的财富几乎不再值得媒体报道了。

sentences.en: One of Gassner's most in-depth profiles was published on the blog of the Hacienda Business Park in Pleasanton, California, where Viva keeps its offices.
sentences.zh: 加斯纳最深入的个人简介之一发表在加利福尼亚州普莱森顿哈仙达商业园的博客上，Viva的办公室就在那里。

sentences.en: He does not own any hot air balloons.
sentences.zh: 他没有拥有任何热气球。

sentences.en: Since 1987, Forbes has published another list, which started smaller but has grown to be much larger, the World's Billionaires LiSt.
sentences.zh: 自1987年以来，《福布斯》又发布了另一份榜单，起初规模较小，但后来发展得大得多，即“全球亿万富翁榜”。

sentences.en: The magazine just published this year's edition, with a staggering 2,668 names.
sentences.zh: 该杂志刚刚发布了今年的版本，名单上的人数达到了惊人的2668人。

sentences.en: The task of gathering information for both lists is overseen by Kerry Dolan, an editor at Forbes,
sentences.zh: 为两份榜单收集信息的任务由《福布斯》编辑克里·多兰负责监督，

sentences.en: in a highly collaborative effort that involves at least 92 different reporters from all over the organization,
sentences.zh: 这是一项高度协作的工作，涉及来自整个组织至少92名不同的记者，

sentences.en: including from the company's many internationally licensed editions, Russia, Poland, India, and more, each a testament to the triumph of globalized capitalism.
sentences.zh: 包括来自该公司许多国际授权版本（俄罗斯、波兰、印度等）的记者，每一位都是全球化资本主义胜利的见证。

sentences.en: Dolan has worked at Forbes for nearly three decades, starting in 1994 covering Latin America, which involved helping out on the Billionaires List too.
sentences.zh: 多兰在《福布斯》工作了近三十年，1994年开始负责报道拉丁美洲，这也包括协助亿万富翁榜的工作。

sentences.en: Compiling it was far more laborious back then.
sentences.zh: 那时编制这份榜单要费力得多。

sentences.en: I couldn't just go online and look at the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange and figure out who owned what, Dolan says,
sentences.zh: “我不能只是上网看看圣保罗证券交易所，就能弄清楚谁拥有什么，”多兰说，

sentences.en: But a financial magazine down in Brazil used to put out a book about all the biggest companies in the country, and she would have a contact in Brazil ship it to her in the States.
sentences.zh: “但巴西的一家财经杂志过去常出版一本关于该国所有大公司的书，她会找巴西的联系人把它寄到美国给她。”

sentences.en: That would reveal financial information on these companies, and she could go from there.
sentences.zh: 那会揭示这些公司的财务信息，她就可以从那里入手。

sentences.en: The process has become easier in one sense, because our access to information is so much better, and harder, because there are so many more billionaires.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这个过程变得更容易了，因为我们获取信息的渠道好多了；但也更难了，因为亿万富翁的数量太多了。

sentences.en: The 2022 World's Billionaires List, for example, grew by 573 names compared with the last pre-pandemic list in 2020.
sentences.zh: 例如，2022年全球亿万富翁榜的人数比2020年疫情前的最后一份榜单增加了573人。

sentences.en: That year, the world was minting new billionaires at a rate, Forbes noted, of about one every 17 hours.
sentences.zh: 那一年，正如《福布斯》指出的，世界以大约每17小时产生一位新亿万富翁的速度在制造亿万富翁。

sentences.en: At the top of the new list is Elon Musk, with an estimated net worth of $219 billion.
sentences.zh: 新榜单榜首是埃隆·马斯克，估计净资产为2190亿美元。

sentences.en: Behind him is Jeff Bezos, with $171 billion.
sentences.zh: 排在他后面的是杰夫·贝佐斯，拥有1710亿美元。

sentences.en: From there, it goes like this.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，排名如下。

sentences.en: Bernard Arnault and family, $158 billion.
sentences.zh: 伯纳德·阿诺特及其家族，1580亿美元。

sentences.en: Bill Gates, $129 billion.
sentences.zh: 比尔·盖茨，1290亿美元。

sentences.en: Warren Buffett, $118 billion.
sentences.zh: 沃伦·巴菲特，1180亿美元。

sentences.en: Larry Page, $111 billion.
sentences.zh: 拉里·佩奇，1110亿美元。

sentences.en: Sergey Brin, $107 billion.
sentences.zh: 谢尔盖·布林，1070亿美元。

sentences.en: Larry Ellison, $106 billion.
sentences.zh: 拉里·埃里森，1060亿美元。

sentences.en: Steve Ballmer, $91.4 billion.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫·鲍尔默，914亿美元。

sentences.en: And Mukesh Umbani, $90.7 billion.
sentences.zh: 以及穆凯什·安巴尼，907亿美元。

sentences.en: The richest man in Asia, and, I confess, the highest-ranked person on the list I'd never heard of.
sentences.zh: 亚洲首富，而且我承认，这是榜单上排名最高但我从未听说过的人。

sentences.en: If you continued down, keeping your eyes on the Americans, most are familiar.
sentences.zh: 如果你继续往下看，关注那些美国人，大多数都很熟悉。

sentences.en: Names you know from the vast fortunes cast off by Silicon Valley, or Walmart.
sentences.zh: 那些名字你从硅谷或沃尔玛创造的巨额财富中都很熟悉。

sentences.en: The wealthiest Walton heirs have around $65 billion each.
sentences.zh: 最富有的沃尔顿家族继承人每人拥有约650亿美元。

sentences.en: Or Nike, $47.3 billion.
sentences.zh: 或者耐克，473亿美元。

sentences.en: Or divorcing Jeff Bezos, $43.6 billion.
sentences.zh: 或者离婚后的杰夫·贝佐斯，436亿美元。

sentences.en: Or living longer than Sheldon Adelson, $27.5 billion.
sentences.zh: 或者比谢尔登·阿德尔森活得久的人，275亿美元。

sentences.en: But eventually, you start to encounter less familiar names.
sentences.zh: 但最终，你会开始遇到一些不太熟悉的名字。

sentences.en: Thomas Petterfi, who immigrated from communist Hungary and pioneered computerized stock trading.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·彼得菲，他从共产主义匈牙利移民而来，开创了计算机化股票交易的先河。

sentences.en: Number 80, $20.1 billion.
sentences.zh: 第80名，201亿美元。

sentences.en: Robert Perra, who founded something called Ubiquity Networks and, this was fun to learn, went to the same state college that I did.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·佩拉，他创立了一家叫Ubiquity Networks的公司，而且——了解到这一点很有趣——他和我上的是同一所州立大学。

sentences.en: Number 127, $14.6 billion.
Speaking of college, there's Dustin Moskovitz, who was roommates at Harvard with another guy who had a cool idea for a social network.
sentences.zh: 说到大学，还有达斯汀·莫斯科维茨，他曾是哈佛大学的室友，而另一个室友对社交网络有个很酷的想法。

sentences.en: Number 167, $11.5 billion.
Before long, you're down with the Peter Gassners of the world.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，你就到了像彼得·加斯纳那样的世界了。

sentences.en: And there are a lot of them.
sentences.zh: 而且这样的人有很多。

sentences.en: America has some 735 billionaires now, according to Forbes, collectively worth more than $4.7 trillion.
sentences.zh: 据《福布斯》统计，美国现在有约735位亿万富翁，总资产超过4.7万亿美元。

sentences.en: A decade ago, Forbes counted only, only, $424.
sentences.zh: 十年前，《福布斯》只统计到424位。

sentences.en: A decade before that, $243.
sentences.zh: 再往前十年，是243位。

sentences.en: They keep multiplying, and their collective wealth grows, even, or especially, as the rest of us fall behind.
sentences.zh: 他们不断繁衍，集体财富不断增长，即使——或者特别是在——我们其他人落后的时候。

sentences.en: So where are they all coming from?
sentences.zh: 那么他们都是从哪里来的呢？

sentences.en: Depends who you ask.
sentences.zh: 这取决于你问谁。

sentences.en: An optimist might tell you that an economy producing so many billionaires is an economy that's growing, which is certainly true of ours.
sentences.zh: 乐观主义者可能会告诉你，一个能产生这么多亿万富翁的经济体是一个正在增长的经济体，这在我们的国家当然是事实。

sentences.en: Nothing wrong with that.
sentences.zh: 这没什么不对。

sentences.en: In the 1950s, the economist Simon Kuznets popularized the idea that inequality was an unfortunate but self-regulating side effect of economic growth.
sentences.zh: 20世纪50年代，经济学家西蒙·库兹涅茨普及了一个观点，即不平等是经济增长中不幸但可以自我调节的副作用。

sentences.en: Whenever it got too high, Kuznets reasoned, the political process would rein it in.
sentences.zh: 库兹涅茨认为，每当不平等程度过高时，政治进程就会对其进行约束。

sentences.en: This was known as the Kuznets Curve, a parabola that showed inequality soaring before being slowly brought back to Earth through redistribution.
sentences.zh: 这就是著名的“库兹涅茨曲线”，一条抛物线，显示不平等在通过再分配缓慢回到地球之前会先飙升。

sentences.en: Kuznets believed that the richest societies would eventually be the most equal.
sentences.zh: 库兹涅茨相信，最富有的社会最终会是最平等的社会。

sentences.en: But in the last 12 years, the American political system has delivered Citizens United, a top marginal tax rate of 37%, down from a high of 94% in Kuznets' day,
sentences.zh: 但在过去12年里，美国政治体系带来了“联合公民诉联邦选举委员会案”的裁决，最高边际税率降至37%（库兹涅茨时代最高为94%），

sentences.en: and a billionaire president openly hostile to the democratic process, along with 332 new billionaires.
sentences.zh: 还有一位公开敌视民主进程的亿万富翁总统，以及332位新亿万富翁。

sentences.en: The Kuznets Curve has fallen out of favor, too, replaced by something called the Kuznets Wave, which shows successive peaks and valleys of inequality.
sentences.zh: 库兹涅茨曲线也不再受宠，取而代之的是所谓的“库兹涅茨波动”，它显示了不平等现象的连续起伏。

sentences.en: Bronko Milanovic, the economist who put forward this revised model, thinks it might take at least a generation to tamp down the current peak.
sentences.zh: 提出这一修正模型的经济学家布兰科·米拉诺维奇认为，可能至少需要一代人的时间才能平抑当前的峰值。

sentences.en: In his book, Ages of American Capitalism, the University of Chicago historian Jonathan Levy describes the era of capitalism we live in
sentences.zh: 芝加哥大学历史学家乔纳森·利维在他的著作《美国资本主义时代》中，将我们所处的资本主义时代描述为

sentences.en: as the age of chaos, a time in which capital has become more footloose, liquid, and volatile, constantly flowing into and out of booms and busts,
sentences.zh: “混乱时代”，一个资本变得更加自由、流动和动荡的时期，不断地在繁荣与萧条之间流动，

sentences.en: in contrast to the staid order and widely shared prosperity that characterized the industrial post-war economy.
sentences.zh: 与工业战后经济所具有的稳重秩序和广泛共享的繁荣形成了鲜明对比。

sentences.en: Levy begins the story in 1981, the same year Forbes thought of his liSt.
sentences.zh: 利维的故事始于1981年，也就是福布斯想到他的榜单的那一年。

sentences.en: That was the year the Federal Reserve, under its chairman Paul Volcker, raised interest rates to 20% with the goal of ending inflation.
sentences.zh: 那一年，美联储在主席保罗·沃尔克的领导下，为了终结通货膨胀，将利率提高到了20%。

sentences.en: Volcker's Fed succeeded at that, but the decision, Levy notes, had far-reaching consequences besides, accelerating America's transition away from the production of goods
sentences.zh: 沃尔克的美联储成功做到了这一点，但利维指出，这一决定还有深远的影响，加速了美国从商品生产向

sentences.en: to a form of capitalism never seen before.
sentences.zh: 一种前所未见的资本主义形式的转型。

sentences.en: The dollar skyrocketed in value, making American exports even less attractive and imports even cheaper.
sentences.zh: 美元价值飙升，使得美国出口产品吸引力下降，进口产品变得更加便宜。

sentences.en: Many factories that remained profitable were closed because, compared with the incredible returns money could earn in such a high-rate environment,
sentences.zh: 许多原本盈利的工厂被关闭，因为与在高利率环境下资金所能获得的惊人回报相比，

sentences.en: they simply weren't profitable enough.
sentences.zh: 它们根本不够赚钱。

sentences.en: When the Fed began to loosen its grip, the widely available credit unleashed a speculative bonanza, which benefited a newly empowered corporate class
sentences.zh: 当美联储开始放松控制时，广泛可用的信贷释放了一场投机狂潮，这使一个新获得权力的企业阶层受益，

sentences.en: that felt little obligation to the workforce and profound obligations to shareholders.
sentences.zh: 他们对劳动力几乎没有义务，却对股东负有深重的义务。

sentences.en: Typically, the economy expands when investments are made in productivity, but this expansion was different.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，当投资于生产力时，经济会扩张，但这次扩张不同。

sentences.en: It was, Levy writes, the only one on record before or since in which fixed investment as a share of GDP declined.
sentences.zh: 利维写道，这是有记录以来唯一一次固定资产投资占GDP份额下降的扩张。

sentences.en: In other words, our industrialists were investing less in productive stuff, ships, factories, trucks, while making more money doing so.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我们的实业家在生产性资产（船只、工厂、卡车）上的投资减少了，同时却赚了更多的钱。

sentences.en: In fact, they were often tearing that stuff up and shipping it abroad.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们经常拆除这些东西并将其运往国外。

sentences.en: This was the age of the corporate raiders, who would book enormous profits while putting Americans out of work.
sentences.zh: 这就是企业掠夺者的时代，他们在让美国人失业的同时，却能获得巨大的利润。

sentences.en: You can see this, in crude terms, as the birth of the Wall Street-Main Street divide, a severing of the finance industry from the real economy.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，你可以把这看作是华尔街与实体经济分道扬镳的开端，金融业从此与实体经济脱钩。

sentences.en: This shift to a highly financialized post-industrial economy was helped along by the Reagan administration, which deregulated banking, cut the top income tax rate to 28% from 70%,
sentences.zh: 这种向高度金融化的后工业经济的转变，得到了里根政府的推波助澜，他们放松了银行业监管，并将最高所得税率从70%削减至28%，

sentences.en: and took aim at organized labor, a political scapegoat for the sluggish inflationary economy of the 70s.
sentences.zh: 同时将矛头指向了有组织劳工，将其作为70年代经济增长缓慢、通胀严重时的政治替罪羊。

sentences.en: Computer technology and the rise of the developing world would amplify and accelerate all these trends, turning the United States into a sort of frontal cortex
sentences.zh: 计算机技术和发展中国家的崛起，进一步放大并加速了所有这些趋势，使美国成为了全球化经济的

sentences.en: for the globalizing economy.
sentences.zh: 某种前额叶皮层。

sentences.en: Just as important, the tech revolution created new ways for entrepreneurs to amass enormous fortunes.
sentences.zh: 同样重要的是，科技革命为企业家积累巨额财富创造了新途径。

sentences.en: Software is by no means cheap to develop, but it requires fewer workers and less fixed investment, and can be reproduced and shipped around the world instantaneously
sentences.zh: 软件开发绝非廉价，但它所需的员工更少，固定资产投资更低，而且可以瞬间在全球范围内复制和分发，

sentences.en: and at practically no coSt.
sentences.zh: 几乎不需要任何成本。

sentences.en: Consider that the powerhouse of 20th century capitalism,
sentences.zh: 想想看，20世纪资本主义的动力源泉，

sentences.en: Ford Motors, now employs about 183,000 people and has a market capitalization close to $68 billion.
sentences.zh: 福特汽车，现在拥有约18.3万名员工，市值接近680亿美元。

sentences.en: Google employs about 156,000 people and has a market cap of around $1.8 trillion.
sentences.zh: 谷歌拥有约15.6万名员工，市值约为1.8万亿美元。

sentences.en: This new economy would be run by and for knowledge workers, who would reap most of the gains and therefore have more money to spend on services,
sentences.zh: 这种新经济将由知识工作者主导并为他们服务，他们将获得大部分收益，因此有更多的钱用于消费服务，

sentences.en: a sector that would come to sort of but never fully replace the manufacturing this transformation did away with.
sentences.zh: 这个行业在某种程度上取代了此次转型所淘汰的制造业，但从未完全取代。

sentences.en: During the Reagan years, Levy writes, something new and distinctive emerged that has persisted down to this day, a capitalism dominated by asset price appreciation.
sentences.zh: 利维写道，在里根执政期间，出现了一种新的、独特的现象，并一直持续至今，那就是由资产价格升值所主导的资本主义。

sentences.en: That is, an economy in which the rising price of assets, stocks, bonds, real estate, would be somewhat counterintuitively a fuel for economic growth.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，在这种经济中，资产、股票、债券、房地产价格的上涨，反直觉地成为了经济增长的燃料。

sentences.en: It has been a good time, in other words, to own a lot of assets.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这是一个拥有大量资产的好时代。

sentences.en: And owning assets is mostly what billionaires do.
sentences.zh: 而拥有资产正是亿万富翁们主要做的事情。

sentences.en: In his book, Capital in the 21st Century, the French economist Thomas Piketty notes that the new economic order has made it difficult for the super-rich not to get richer.
sentences.zh: 法国经济学家托马斯·皮凯蒂在他的著作《21世纪资本论》中指出，新的经济秩序使得超级富豪们很难不变得更富有。

sentences.en: Past a certain threshold, he writes, all large fortunes, whether inherited or entrepreneurial in origin, grow at extremely high rates,
sentences.zh: 他写道，一旦超过某个门槛，所有巨额财富，无论是继承而来还是白手起家，都会以极高的速度增长，

sentences.en: regardless of whether the owner of the fortune works or not.
sentences.zh: 无论财富的所有者是否工作。

sentences.en: He uses the examples of Bill Gates and Lillian Bettencourt, the heiress to the L'Oreal fortune.
sentences.zh: 他以比尔·盖茨和欧莱雅财富继承人莉莉安·贝当古为例。

sentences.en: Bettencourt never worked a day in her life,
sentences.zh: 贝当古一生中从未工作过一天，

sentences.en: Piketty writes, but her fortune and Gates's each grew by an annual rate of about 13% from 1990 to 2010.
sentences.zh: 皮凯蒂写道，但从1990年到2010年，她和盖茨的财富每年都以约13%的速度增长。

sentences.en: Once a fortune is established, the capital grows according to a dynamic of its own,
sentences.zh: 皮凯蒂指出，一旦财富积累到一定程度，资本就会按照其自身的动力增长，

sentences.en: Piketty notes, adding that bigger fortunes tend to grow faster.
sentences.zh: 并补充说，越大的财富往往增长得越快。

sentences.en: No matter how extravagant, their owner's living expenses are still such a small proportion of the returns that even more is left over for reinvestment.
sentences.zh: 无论多么奢侈，所有者的生活开支在收益中所占比例微乎其微，以至于剩下的钱更多地用于再投资。

sentences.en: Piketty was writing in 2013, while the economy was still recovering from the financial crisis of 2008.
sentences.zh: 皮凯蒂写这本书时是2013年，当时经济正处于从2008年金融危机中复苏的过程中。

sentences.en: That recovery was buoyed by several years of near-zero interest rates, kept there by the Fed on the theory that, with credit widely available, the economy would regain its health.
sentences.zh: 那次复苏得益于美联储维持了数年的近零利率，其理论是，在信贷广泛可用的情况下，经济将恢复健康。

sentences.en: But low interest rates do two things.
sentences.zh: 但低利率会带来两件事。

sentences.en: They push investors into riskier territory, seeking better returns, and ideally creating jobs in the process, and they inflate the value of assets.
sentences.zh: 它们迫使投资者进入风险更高的领域以寻求更好的回报，并在此过程中理想地创造就业机会，同时它们也会推高资产价值。

sentences.en: Private equity and venture capital benefited greatly from this low-rate environment, helping both Silicon Valley and the financial engineers of Wall Street clean up once more.
sentences.zh: 私募股权和风险投资从这种低利率环境中获益匪浅，再次帮助硅谷和华尔街的金融工程师们大赚了一笔。

sentences.en: Even in less dynamic sectors of the economy, the cheap money enabled an explosion in stock buybacks, some $6.3 trillion worth during the 2010s,
sentences.zh: 即使在经济中活力较弱的部门，廉价资金也促成了股票回购的激增，2010年代回购总额约为6.3万亿美元，

sentences.en: or about 4% of our GDP over the same period, more than we currently spend on defense.
sentences.zh: 约占我们同期GDP的4%，超过了我们目前的国防开支。

sentences.en: This, too, made asset owners richer.
sentences.zh: 这也让资产所有者变得更加富有。

sentences.en: The Trump years supercharged another bull market that would be supercharged again, paradoxically, by the COVID pandemic.
sentences.zh: 特朗普执政时期进一步助推了牛市，而讽刺的是，新冠疫情又再次推高了这一行情。

sentences.en: When the Fed and Congress stepped in to prop up markets and assist the economy, they fueled yet another boom in asset prices, this time with more everyday Americans
sentences.zh: 当美联储和国会介入以支撑市场并援助经济时，他们又一次引发了资产价格的繁荣，这一次更多的普通美国人

sentences.en: trying to get a piece of it, investing in everything from Tesla options to JPEGs of apes.
sentences.zh: 试图分一杯羹，投资于从特斯拉期权到猿猴图片（JPEG）的各种资产。

sentences.en: The retail investors have seen winners and losers among them, while the billionaire class as a whole has absolutely flourished.
sentences.zh: 散户投资者中既有赢家也有输家，而亿万富翁阶层作为一个整体则绝对是蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: Over the last five years,
sentences.zh: 在过去五年里，

sentences.en: Jeff Bezos' fortune has more than doubled.
sentences.zh: 杰夫·贝佐斯的财富翻了一倍多。

sentences.en: Elon Musk's, fueled in part by retail investor exuberance, has grown by a factor of 20.
sentences.zh: 埃隆·马斯克的财富在散户投资者狂热的推动下，增长了20倍。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·罗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重塑者》，这是一档关于对设计的热爱以及围绕设计的文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs, in the era of vinyl, every night, you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，每天晚上，你都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，然后把DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成一个活生生的、快闪式的精美50年历史文物博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet and now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听爱彼赞助的《重塑者》，现已在您最喜爱的播客平台上架。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th,
I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 我将在纽约市的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、

sentences.en: Christine Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼等等。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无保留、未经修饰的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过NYTimes.com免费直播精选采访，供所有人观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，阅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Nothing special happens when you become a billionaire.
sentences.zh: 当你成为亿万富翁时，并不会发生什么特别的事情。

sentences.en: There isn't a little red light that flips on at IRS headquarters.
sentences.zh: 美国国税局总部也不会亮起什么小红灯。

sentences.en: At the low end, it's not even a stable status.
sentences.zh: 在低端，这甚至不是一个稳定的身份。

sentences.en: Market fluctuations push people in and out of billionaire-dom every day.
sentences.zh: 市场波动每天都在把人们推入或挤出亿万富翁的行列。

sentences.en: What's incredible is how little information we have a right to know about them, these 735 Americans who have amassed, at minimum, the GDP of a small island nation.
sentences.zh: 令人难以置信的是，我们对他们知之甚少，这735名美国人积累的财富至少相当于一个小岛国的GDP。

sentences.en: We can know only what they share or can't hide from journalists, and certainly some are better at hiding than others.
sentences.zh: 我们只能知道他们愿意分享或无法向记者隐瞒的信息，当然，有些人比其他人更擅长隐藏。

sentences.en: I asked Dolan what her profile is of a billionaire whom she'd never find.
sentences.zh: 我问多兰，她心目中那种永远无法被发现的亿万富翁是什么样的。

sentences.en: She told me it's someone who quietly sold a stake in a business for, say, $250 million in the 90s, then invested it well.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，那是一个在90年代悄悄卖掉了一家公司股份，比如卖了2.5亿美元，然后投资得当的人。

sentences.en: Today, a guy like that could use his wealth to do whatever he wanted, buy truckloads of Nazi memorabilia, try to persuade your mayor to privatize the city's sewers, or maybe both,
